title: Completed ell-power reduction preserves integral constructibility
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a Noetherian scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. For the normalized coefficient-tower interface $D$ and reduction construction $R$ of [det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized], transport reduction to the completed coefficient derived category as in [lem-sp-completed-tower-roos]. If $M$ satisfies $\operatorname{sfIntegralConstructible}$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], then its transported reduction satisfies $\operatorname{spNormalizedConstructibleTorTowers}$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]: all levels have bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude with one common cohomological interval and one common Tor interval, and every actual reduction map is invertible.

source.place: Adjunction, Unit, Counit and Restriction paragraphs; Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 3.5.7

proof.text: Unpack integral constructibility: all positive uniformizer reductions are intrinsically constructible in one common cohomological interval. Intrinsic finite torsion constructibility uses the same stratification and finite stalks as the pro-etale predicate.

Apply the residue Tor theorem to a common interval containing residue cohomology. It provides one Tor interval for every uniformizer reduction. Write ell as a unit times pi^e and select levels e(n+1); the quotient ring isomorphisms preserve constructibility, cohomological bounds and Tor amplitude.

The derived evaluation comparisons of R identify the selected reductions with the actual completed reduction tower. Its transitions are normalized by R.normalized. These are precisely the two conjuncts of the normalized constructible finite-Tor tower predicate.
